stem: In children aged 6 to 11 years, which symptom pattern is consistent with persistent asthma?

options.text: Waking overnight due to asthma symptoms more than twice per month
Having symptoms that occur less than once every six weeks
Experiencing one mild flare-up per year requiring only salbutamol
Daytime symptoms occurring exactly once per month
Using salbutamol only before exercise with no other symptoms

explanation: Persistent asthma is suggested by waking overnight due to asthma symptoms more than twice per month, which indicates ongoing poor control.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because waking overnight due to asthma symptoms more than twice per month is a feature of persistent asthma in this age group.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because symptoms this infrequent are more consistent with intermittent asthma.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a single mild flare-up per year does not by itself meet criteria for persistent asthma.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because symptoms once per month are not the typical frequency used to define persistent asthma.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because exercise-only symptoms without other features do not define persistent asthma.

source.hint: Look for a frequency of nighttime disturbances that indicates the disease is not adequately controlled.
